rows.notes: The study is a perspective/opinion letter (ERL 'Letter') arguing that the idea that modern irrigation technologies save water is a 'zombie idea'. It reports no primary data, experiment, survey or model runs of its own; its only quantitative content (figure 2: 230 case studies, 70.4% reduced water availability elsewhere, 11.2% saved water) is reproduced from the authors' earlier literature review (P<U+00E9>rez-Blanco et al 2020), and the rest is conceptual argument drawing on cited literature (Quiggin, Krugman, Peters and Nagel, Lewandowsky etc.). Statements that altered return flows reduce downstream water availability and complicate governance (section 2, figure 1 caption, section 3.3) are assertions and citations, not the study's own results. Q1 is therefore 'no' and all subsequent questions 'no'.
